parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The file declares `CreateOrderDto`, a plain input shape. Its only extra content is structural and format checks from class-validator (`@IsString`, `@IsOptional`, `@IsEmail`). The layer model assigns `*.dto.ts` files to the application layer, and defining the input contract for a use case is that layer's role. The command and the service in the same use case consume this class.

The file has no persistence, no HTTP handling, no routing and no framework wiring. It contains no business rules or domain invariants either. The doc comment calls the class a "transport contract" and mentions `ValidationPipe` and HTTP 400. That is a description, not logic: the code itself stays HTTP-agnostic. `@IsEmail` is a format check on input, not a business rule.

One point is debatable. Some teams would keep transport-specific validation in a presentation-layer request DTO and give the application layer an undecorated one. This file carries no behaviour that would make that separation required, so I did not count it as a violation.
